name: Hypopigmentation of the skin

ethnicAssociations: More noticeable in individuals with darker skin tones

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis based on dermatological assessment

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated hypopigmented or depigmented macules or patches on the skin
Wood's lamp examination showing accentuation of hypopigmented areas
Lack of significant inflammatory signs in affected skin areas
Skin biopsy demonstrating decreased or absent melanin pigment and melanocytes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic hypopigmented patches confirmed by Wood's lamp examination; histopathology supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; biopsy reserved for atypical cases or to exclude other causes

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic sharply defined lighter skin patches

pathognomonic.symptomName: Depigmented skin patches with accentuation under Wood's lamp
searchTerms: white skin patches glowing under UV light
depigmented areas visible with Wood's lamp
skin spots lighter under special light

common.symptomName: Absence of erythema or scaling in affected areas
searchTerms: no redness or scaling in pale areas
absence of skin inflammation on patches

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to hypopigmented patches
searchTerms: mild itching on pale skin patches

common.symptomName: Slow progression of hypopigmentation over months to years
common.notes: Gradual enlargement or increase in number of patches
searchTerms: slowly spreading pale skin over years

occasional.symptomName: Associated hair depigmentation (poliosis) in affected areas
occasional.notes: Localized white hair patches may occur
searchTerms: white hair patches in affected skin
hair color loss near pale spots
skin sensitive to sunlight in pale areas
mild sun sensitivity on hypopigmented skin
light skin patches prone to sun discomfort

occasional.symptomName: Psychological distress related to cosmetic appearance
occasional.notes: Emotional impact due to visible skin changes
searchTerms: psychological impact of cosmetic skin changes
mental health issues due to visible skin patches

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial colonization of hypopigmented areas
searchTerms: secondary infections in light skin spots
skin losing pigment similar to vitiligo
pale skin with numbness or tingling

laboratory: Autoimmune panel if associated autoimmune disease suspected
imaging: Wood's lamp examination highlighting hypopigmented areas
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; familial cases rare
other: Skin biopsy showing decreased melanin and melanocytes

distinguishingFeatures: History of preceding skin inflammation or injury

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
references: Taieb A, Picardo M. Clinical practice. Vitiligo. N Engl J Med. 2009;360(2):160-169.
